name: dropdown-menu
pattern: An action menu opened by the WAI-ARIA APG Menu Button Pattern and context actions
responsibility: Provides menu opening and closing, item focus and keyboard operations, ARIA, item selection, and context-action coordinates. Does not generate positioning, appearance, submenus, or item content

targets.trigger: One native <button type="button"> with data-dropdown-menu-target="trigger" inside the root
targets.menu: One native <menu> with data-dropdown-menu-target="menu" inside the root
targets.item: Zero or more native <button type="button"> elements with data-dropdown-menu-target="item" inside the menu. Each item may have a non-empty data-dropdown-menu-value
targets.context: Zero or one optional HTMLElement region. It is a root descendant other than the root itself, does not contain the menu, and is not inside the menu. The user supplies the region's role, name, and focusability according to its meaning. A trigger remains required in this configuration

authorMarkup.label: Give the trigger and menu items names through text content, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Name the menu with aria-label or aria-labelledby; when omitted, supplement aria-labelledby referencing the trigger. The rules for text-based names are the same as toggle-group
authorMarkup.validity: Markup with exactly one trigger target and one menu target in a root is valid author markup. Navigation links, listboxes, select-only comboboxes, and submenus are outside the action-menu scope
authorMarkup.positioning: The user owns menu position, z-index, backdrop, and transition in CSS. Output viewport coordinates as CSS custom properties only when a context target exists. Do not provide a top layer
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements, items, or content

semanticElements: The trigger must be a native <button type="button">
The menu must be a native <menu>
An item must be a native <button type="button"> descendant of the menu

There must be zero or one context target, an HTMLElement that is a root descendant and does not contain the menu or reside inside it. Disable enhancement when the trigger or an item has an empty name, or an explicitly supplied menu name is empty
contractValidation.allowedRoles: Allow menu role only when omitted or menu; trigger aria-haspopup only when omitted, menu, or true; and item role only when omitted or menuitem. Any other authored role or aria-haspopup violates the action-menu contract
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate semanticElements and allowedRoles on connection and operation or target replacement. For markup that is invalid from the start, do not set ARIA, state, hidden, or focus and issue one warning while connected. If a previously valid configuration becomes invalid, synchronize an open menu to closed, clean up long-press tracking, context, and coordinates, and disable later operations. Do not move focus
contractValidation.warning: The warning includes the violating element type, role, and controller name. Validate again after the user repairs the markup and reconnects

attributes: aria-labelledby referencing the trigger when the menu has no name
completion.warning: The completion warning lists the added attributes: "Added <attributes>. Include them in your markup." It is emitted once while connected, using a separate flag from the enhancement-disabled warning

contractValidation.completionExempt: Add trigger / menu / item ids, state and focus output, and context-configuration coordinate custom properties without warnings. The user owns static context role, name, and tabindex because their meaning cannot be determined

open.description: Current open state. The setter commits state without dispatching an event or moving focus

show().description: Open programmatically without changing initial focus or dispatching an event

hide().description: Close programmatically without changing focus or dispatching an event

toggle().description: Toggle open programmatically without changing focus or dispatching an event

select(value).description: Select a known enabled item by value and close the menu without dispatching an event. Unknown, empty, and disabled values are no-ops

dropdown-menu:beforeopen.when: Immediately before opening from trusted trigger activation or a context action, or changing the context of an open menu

detail.context: The HTMLElement where the context action started. Absent when opened from an ordinary button or the API

dropdown-menu:beforeopen.effect: When preventDefault() is called, do not open or move focus

dropdown-menu:open.when: After opening from trusted trigger activation or a context action, or committing a context change

detail.context: The HTMLElement where the context action started. Absent when opened from an ordinary button or the API

dropdown-menu:beforeclose.when: Immediately before close from trusted Escape, outside pointer, Tab, trigger toggle, or item selection

detail.value: The value when item selection initiated the close; otherwise an empty string
detail.context: The HTMLElement where the context action started. Absent when opened from an ordinary button or the API

dropdown-menu:beforeclose.effect: When preventDefault() is called, keep the menu open; for item selection, do not commit selection or close

dropdown-menu:close.when: After a trusted close is committed

detail.value: The value when item selection initiated the close; otherwise an empty string
detail.context: The HTMLElement where the context action started. Absent when opened from an ordinary button or the API

dropdown-menu:select.when: After trusted item activation commits without beforeclose cancellation and the menu closes

detail.context: The HTMLElement where the context action started. Absent when opened from an ordinary button or the API

events.programmatic: The open setter, show(), hide(), toggle(), select(value), initialization, dynamic target synchronization, and disconnect/reconnect do not dispatch events

customProperties.--dropdown-menu-x: The viewport-relative x coordinate (px) output on the root in a context configuration
customProperties.--dropdown-menu-y: The viewport-relative y coordinate (px) output on the root in a context configuration

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Specify data-action="dropdown-menu:select->controller#method dropdown-menu:close->controller#method" on the root or an ancestor. Ordinary item click actions can also be used; the controller does not stop event propagation
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: To stop close, call event.preventDefault() with data-action="dropdown-menu:beforeclose->controller#method". Item selection canceled by beforeclose dispatches neither select nor close
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Another controller can call open/show/hide/toggle/select through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. APIs called programmatically do not dispatch events
consumerIntegration.nested: When receiving events from a nested menu outside, narrow them to your root with the data-action :self modifier or event.target === event.currentTarget

behavior.initial: Synchronize menu hidden, trigger aria-expanded, and state output from the open value. Do not move focus for initial open
behavior.trigger: A trusted click toggles open/close with pointer or keyboard reason. Ignore disabled triggers
behavior.item: A trusted click on an enabled item commits its value with pointer reason, then performs close and dropdown-menu:select through beforeclose. Ignore disabled items
behavior.outside: A pointerdown outside the root while open closes through beforeclose with pointer reason. Do not treat it as outside when root appears in composedPath()
behavior.lightDismiss: The controller handles Escape and outside pointerdown. Do not depend on the popover attribute or browser light dismiss
behavior.positioning: Output --dropdown-menu-x / --dropdown-menu-y on the root only in a context configuration. Pointer actions use clientX / clientY; keyboard and trigger / API actions use the target rect's bottom and logical start (left in LTR, right in RTL). Commit coordinates when opening; CSS and the user own scroll following, clamping, and placement
behavior.selection: Output value only in event detail; the controller does not store the user's selection. select(value) temporarily synchronizes the selected item's data-state and closes
behavior.context: Open from a trusted contextmenu, Shift+F10, or an unmodified ContextMenu key in the context region. Exclude editing regions of input / textarea / select / contenteditable and menu items. Do not open when the trigger is disabled. A further context action on an open menu updates its target and coordinates through beforeopen
behavior.longPress: Prefer native contextmenu. When no native event occurs, open on release after at least 600ms from a primary touch / pen within 8px of the start position. Cancel on movement, pointercancel, leaving the region, another pointer, or configuration changes. Suppress the compatibility click immediately after accepting a long press. Do not block short taps or scrolling and do not use a timer. Suppress the compatibility click with preventDefault and stopImmediatePropagation in root capture to prevent duplicate user click actions
behavior.nativeMenu: Call preventDefault on native contextmenu only when accepting a request to open the menu. A canceled beforeopen preserves the prior open state and coordinates and does not block the native menu. Stop default behavior when recognizing a keyboard shortcut and do not reopen from the native event after beforeopen cancellation. Distinguish this from a directly received contextmenu event. Do not alter OS/browser operations that do not dispatch contextmenu, such as Firefox Shift+right-click
behavior.reentrancy: Respect API, settings, target, and connection changes made by before listeners and do not commit an old request. Do not continue an old focus move when an after listener changes state

trigger.Enter: Open the menu and focus the first enabled item
trigger.Space: Open the menu and focus the first enabled item
trigger.ArrowDown: Open the menu and focus the first enabled item
trigger.ArrowUp: Open the menu and focus the last enabled item

menu.ArrowDown: Focus the next enabled item; wrap to the first at the end
menu.ArrowUp: Focus the previous enabled item; wrap to the last at the start
menu.Enter: Select the focused item with keyboard reason
menu.Space: Select the focused item with keyboard reason
menu.Escape: Close the menu and return focus to the trigger
menu.Tab: Close through beforeclose and do not prevent default Tab movement

keyboard.optional: Typeahead, submenus, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, menuitemcheckbox, and menuitemradio are outside the scope

context.Shift+F10: Open from the focused element in the context region or from the trigger
context.ContextMenu: Perform the same operation without modifiers
context.IME: Do not process keydown with isComposing / keyCode 229

focus.openByKeyboard: When opened with trigger Enter, Space, ArrowDown, or ArrowUp, focus the specified first or last enabled item
focus.openByPointer: When opened by a pointer click, also focus the first enabled item
focus.close: After close from Escape, item selection, outside pointer, or trigger toggle, return focus when the trigger remains connected and enabled. Do not prevent default focus movement for Tab close
focus.empty: When no enabled item exists, open the menu without moving focus to an item and keep focus on the trigger
focus.context: For context actions, remember the element focused in the region when opening and return focus there after Escape or selection. Return to the trigger when the target is disconnected, disabled, or hidden. Do not add a new tabindex to the context region
focus.reentrancy: Respect focus moved outside by before listeners and state or focus changes made by after listeners

trigger: When aria-haspopup is absent, add aria-haspopup="menu"
Synchronize aria-expanded with the open state as a controller-owned state output
When aria-controls is absent, add the menu id
menu: When role is absent, add role="menu"
When id is absent, add an id unique within the document
Synchronize hidden with the open state as a controller-owned state output
When no name is supplied, reference the trigger id with aria-labelledby
item: When role is absent, add role="menuitem"
Synchronize enabled items to tabindex -1 as a controller-owned focus output
When id is absent, add an id unique within the document
managedMarkup.preservation: Do not overwrite an authored id, role, aria-haspopup, aria-controls, aria-expanded, or other attribute. Synchronize only the completion of a missing controller-owned role, hidden, aria-expanded, tabindex, and data-state
managedMarkup.disabled: Read native :disabled on items and triggers, including disabled state inherited from fieldset. Do not add data-* attributes for disabled state
managedMarkup.context: Do not write role, tabindex, class, or layout style. Own root --dropdown-menu-x / --dropdown-menu-y only while connected, and restore authored values when the context target is removed or on disconnect

stateOutputs.ownership: Root, trigger, menu, and item data-state, trigger aria-expanded, menu hidden, and item tabindex are controller-owned
stateOutputs.item: The focused enabled item has data-state="active" and others have data-state="inactive". Disabled items always have data-state="disabled" and are excluded from focus and selection

lifecycle: Register trigger, menu, and item listeners and the root document pointerdown listener in connect(), and remove them in disconnect(). Do not register twice after reconnection
In disconnect(), remove the document listener and synchronize a menu to closed state without dispatching an event even when it is open
Leave generated attributes and state outputs in place on disconnect().
Track trigger, menu, and item additions and removals with Stimulus TargetConnected/TargetDisconnected
Do not throw when a target is temporarily absent.

Remove root contextmenu / pointerdown / pointermove / pointerup / pointercancel / pointerleave listeners and long-press tracking on disconnect. Discard an in-progress long press when context, trigger, or menu is replaced
acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.

Use native <button> + <menu> + menuitem buttons for the action menu; role=menu, role=menuitem, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and the focus model conform to the APG Menu Button Pattern and WCAG 2.2 Level AA
Detect semantic HTML violations and authored role/aria-haspopup that conflict with an action menu using console.warn and disabled enhancement
The controller does not own menu position, appearance, backdrop, top layer, submenus, or typeahead
Only trusted open/close/item-selection operations honor before-event cancellation and dispatch one committed event in the defined order
The public API, initialization, dynamic target synchronization, and disconnect/reconnect do not dispatch events
Disabled triggers/items are excluded from pointer and keyboard operations; only enabled items are focusable and selectable
Focus return after Escape, outside pointer, Tab, and item selection conforms to the contract
Preserve existing id and ARIA attributes, and ensure generated ids do not collide within the same document
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
Report macOS + Safari + VoiceOver role, menu-item, focus, open/close, and selection-notification checks as unverified when not performed
The context configuration supports every operation through right-click, long press, keyboard, and a persistent button click/tap. It does not move focus with a timer
Verify long-press gesture conditions, native-menu preservation, coordinates, context detail, focus return, before/after reentrancy, and cleanup in all three engines
Treat real-device touch and screen-reader checks as observations and retain them in the completion report when unverified

observations.item: Interaction between native contextmenu and OS selection. Cancel custom long press on pointercancel and use a tap on the persistent button
observations.impact: The public specification is defined by delivered native events and Pointer Events conditions; the persistent button opens the same menu in environments without long-press support

observations.item: Announcements for context actions and returning to the original operation target
observations.impact: The contract is based on menu/button semantics and DOM focus and does not depend on announcement wording
